sources.entry: Sonic Pi - The live coding music synth.

summary.name: Sonic Pi
summary.one_liner: Sonic Pi is a free, open source code-based music creation and live performance tool that lets you make music by writing code.
use_cases: music education for blind and partially sighted people
summary.what_it_does: Sonic Pi is a code-based music tool where synths, samples and effects are controlled by code. Users write live loops, melodies and rhythms, using features such as with_fx reverb and random scale selection. The web version runs in a browser with nothing to install, and the desktop app runs offline on Windows, macOS and Linux. The app supports multichannel audio, low-latency audio interfaces (ASIO, Core Audio, PipeWire), MIDI, OSC, Ableton Link and gamepad input, while the web version has more limited IO. The project is open source, developed since 2012 by over 200 contributors, and originally began as a Cambridge University research project with Raspberry Pi.
notable: Synths, samples and FX are controlled entirely through code, with deterministic randomness so programs play identically each time
Web version runs in the browser on computers, tablets and phones with nothing to install
Used in live performances, school settings, a Royal Albert Hall event and a music played aboard the International Space Station
caveats: Web version lacks low-latency audio interface support, OSC, Ableton Link and works only online
App version is needed for offline use and advanced IO features
Page asks for voluntary community support ('keep it free'), not a required payment
